name: Conduct due diligence on real estate, infrastructure and energy investments
summary: A Real Assets deal team takes an opportunity that passed screening into deep diligence: a property or portfolio bought with a joint venture partner, an infrastructure company, or a power, renewables or energy business. The team assesses the partner, reviews the data room, visits the assets, builds a cash flow model that runs 10 to 30 years, hires engineering, environmental, market, legal and insurance advisers, negotiates governance rights with the partner and gets tax and sustainability and climate input before writing the investment memo for Risk and the Portfolio Execution Committee. About half of these deals reach a memo; the rest are dropped on technical, regulatory or price grounds or lost. Adviser reports, seller answers and partner negotiations take most of the elapsed time, and memos go through several rounds of edits.

baseline.org_archetype: A very large Canadian public pension investment manager whose Real Assets department of about 250 people holds about 200 real estate, infrastructure and energy investments, mostly with partners.
baseline.notes: Real estate is done mostly through joint ventures with existing operating partners; infrastructure and energy deals buy significant stakes with governance rights, often alongside other investors.

trigger: The group head accepts a screening memo and the team enters the second round of a sale process or a partner brings a bilateral deal.
end_state: An investment memo is submitted to Risk and the Portfolio Execution Committee, or the deal is dropped or lost.

volume.seasonality: Fewer new processes in summer and December; COVID-19 slowed deal activity in 2020.

evidence.note: Process map volume derived from the published deal funnel (23.7 of 100 opportunities reach deep diligence). Likely high: Real Assets added a net 25 investments in F2021 (179 to 204).

roles.title: Senior Managing Director, Global Head of Real Assets and Chief Sustainability Officer

evidence.note: Chairs the department investment review. Estimated from hands-on time per deal times about 25 deals a month in deep diligence.

systems.name: Deal pipeline and relationship management system
Virtual data rooms run by sellers and advisors
Bloomberg terminals, market data and trade messaging
Document management and investment committee memo repository
Compliance system for personal trading, attestations and restricted lists

steps.name: Staff the deal team and set the diligence workplan
steps.description: After the group head accepts the screening memo, the director names the principal, associates and analyst, sets the diligence timetable against the seller's process letter or the partner's timetable, drafts an adviser budget and records the deal stage in the pipeline system.

evidence.note: Auction round 2 timetable set by the seller. Times are the author's estimates for a mid-sized real estate, infrastructure or energy deal.

steps.name: Clear conflicts and add the target to the watch list
steps.description: A compliance officer checks the target, seller and proposed partner against existing holdings and the restricted list, adds the target to the watch list and confirms the information barrier before the team receives non-public data.

control.basis: Code of Conduct and confidential information policy: watch list entry before receiving material non-public information

evidence.note: Standard watch list practice; the same control appears in the organisation's private equity diligence workflow.

steps.name: Assess the operating or joint venture partner
steps.description: The principal reviews the proposed partner's track record, alignment of interest, fee and promote terms, team, reporting quality and know-your-counterparty documents; for existing partners this is a refresh of the last review.

evidence.note: Real Estate invests through joint ventures with 58 to 60 operating partners and did more than 98% of its F2021 investment with existing partners. Times are the author's estimates for a mid-sized real estate, infrastructure or energy deal.

steps.name: Engage technical, environmental, market and insurance advisers
steps.description: The principal asks engineering, environmental, market, insurance and accounting firms for scopes and fees, compares proposals, negotiates caps and signs engagement letters within the deal's approved transaction cost budget.

control.basis: Expense management policy: seniority-based approval of transaction costs

evidence.note: Investors coordinate an independent engineer, tax, real estate and transaction counsel, environmental consultants and financial advisers. Times are the author's estimates for a mid-sized real estate, infrastructure or energy deal.

steps.name: Scope legal diligence and instruct external counsel
steps.description: In-house legal counsel agrees the legal scope (title and land rights, concessions and licences, permits, material contracts, existing joint venture agreements) and materiality thresholds, and instructs the external law firm.

evidence.note: Title, survey, zoning and contract review are standard legal workstreams. Times are the author's estimates for a mid-sized real estate, infrastructure or energy deal.

steps.name: Review the data room and log questions
steps.description: The associate reads the information memorandum, rent rolls and leases or offtake and concession contracts, operating history, capital expenditure records and regulatory filings in the virtual data room, notes gaps and builds the question list by workstream.

error.defect_description: A material lease, contract or permit term is missed.

evidence.note: A renewable project is several hundred contracts and documents. Times are the author's estimates for a mid-sized real estate, infrastructure or energy deal.

steps.name: Submit questions and chase answers
steps.description: The analyst loads the questions into the data room question module, tracks open items in a spreadsheet by workstream and chases the seller's adviser for overdue answers.

evidence.note: Data room Q&A in round 2. Times are the author's estimates for a mid-sized real estate, infrastructure or energy deal.

steps.name: Wait for seller answers and added documents
steps.description: The seller's adviser and the asset's managers answer questions in batches and upload further documents; sometimes the seller narrows the field or pauses the process.

next.condition: seller drops the fund or halts the sale

evidence.note: Round 2 runs 4 to 6 weeks; answer turnaround is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Visit the assets and meet management or the partner
steps.description: The principal and director tour the main properties or plants, meet management or the operating partner, test the business plan and capital needs on site, and write up notes and new questions.

evidence.note: Management meetings in round 2; 66% of RA professionals sit in international offices close to assets (src2). Times are the author's estimates for a mid-sized real estate, infrastructure or energy deal.

steps.name: Build the long-term cash flow model
steps.description: The associate builds the asset model: leases and re-leasing for real estate, or contracted and regulated revenue, operating costs and capital programmes for infrastructure and energy, over 10 to 30 years or the concession term, with the capital structure, exit or terminal value and sensitivities.

error.defect_description: Indexation, lease expiry or capex timing modelled wrongly.

evidence.note: Real assets are long-term, capital-intensive businesses with predictable, inflation-linked cash flows. Times are the author's estimates for a mid-sized real estate, infrastructure or energy deal.

steps.name: Review the model and challenge assumptions
steps.description: The senior associate walks through the model with the associate, challenges rent growth, capitalisation rates, regulated returns, availability and degradation assumptions against diligence findings and comparables, and lists changes.

evidence.note: Times are the author's estimates for a mid-sized real estate, infrastructure or energy deal.

steps.name: Receive advisers' draft technical, environmental and market reports
steps.description: The engineering firm delivers its property condition assessment or independent engineer's report with a capital replacement budget, the environmental firm its Phase I report (with a Phase II plan if needed), and the market and insurance advisers their findings.

evidence.note: Report scopes from the sources; durations are the author's estimates within the 180-day and one-year windows for Phase I elements.

steps.name: Review advisers' reports and update the model
steps.description: The senior associate reads each report, lists red flags (deferred maintenance, contamination, permit or concession gaps, grid or offtake risk), quantifies capital and remediation costs with the advisers and updates the model and price range.

error.defect_description: A remediation or capital cost is understated.

evidence.note: Times are the author's estimates for a mid-sized real estate, infrastructure or energy deal.

steps.name: Assess operations and draft the value creation plan
steps.description: For a platform or operating company, a Portfolio Value Creation principal reviews operations, management capability and digital opportunities, and drafts the first value creation plan and the governance rights the fund should seek.

evidence.note: PVC assists in due diligence across the deal life cycle. Share of platform deals is the author's estimate from 43 infrastructure and energy investments against 152 real estate investments (F2021).

steps.name: Decide whether to continue after confirmatory findings
steps.description: The group head meets the team, reviews red flags, the updated value range, partner terms and the competitive position, and decides whether to keep spending on the deal.

next.condition: dropped on red flags or price
lost to another bidder or partner walks

evidence.note: About 26% of deep-diligence deals close and 57% reach a signed letter of intent in the survey; branch shares set so about 55% of deals reach a memo.

steps.name: Prepare the term sheet and send it to Tax and Sustainable Investing
steps.description: The senior associate writes the proposed structure, price, partner and governance terms and jurisdictions into a term sheet and sends it to the tax team for structuring and to Sustainable Investing for the sustainability and climate review.

evidence.note: Sustainable Investing evaluates potential direct investments; tax structuring is a separate process. Times are the author's estimates for a mid-sized real estate, infrastructure or energy deal.

steps.name: Negotiate governance and joint venture terms with the partner
steps.description: The group head negotiates board and committee seats, reserved matters such as business plan approval and new debt, fees and promote, transfer and exit rights, and deadlock provisions with the partner or co-investors.

evidence.note: Reserved matters and deadlock mechanisms are standard joint venture terms; Infrastructure seeks meaningful governance rights. Times are the author's estimates for a mid-sized real estate, infrastructure or energy deal.

steps.name: Review legal findings and mark up the agreements
steps.description: Legal counsel reviews the external firm's title, permit and contract findings, settles the purchase agreement markup and the joint venture or shareholder agreement term sheet for the final bid, and flags issues for the memo.

control.basis: Legal department review of transaction documents before a binding offer

evidence.note: Times are the author's estimates for a mid-sized real estate, infrastructure or energy deal.

steps.name: Confirm asset-level financing and insurance terms
steps.description: The principal confirms debt terms with lenders or the partner (amount, tenor, covenants, hedging) and insurance cover for property damage, business interruption and liability with the broker, and adds both to the model.

evidence.note: Insurance and financial advisers appear in the adviser set; times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Integrate the tax structure memo and the sustainability and climate assessment
steps.description: The associate waits for the tax structure memo and the Sustainable Investing assessment, adds withholding and structure costs to the model, runs the high-physical and high-transition climate scenarios where material, and inserts the findings into the memo draft.
outputs: model with tax and climate cases

control.basis: Climate Change Security Selection Framework: bookend scenarios required where climate impacts are material to a transaction needing committee approval

evidence.note: Climate Change Security Selection Framework with bookend scenarios for material transactions. Times are the author's estimates for a mid-sized real estate, infrastructure or energy deal.

steps.name: Set the valuation range and bid price
steps.description: The director reviews the final model, returns against the hurdle for the strategy, sensitivities and the competitive picture, and sets the recommended price and walk-away level.
inputs: model with tax and climate cases

evidence.note: Times are the author's estimates for a mid-sized real estate, infrastructure or energy deal.

steps.name: Draft the investment memo
steps.description: The senior associate and associate write the memo: thesis, asset and market, partner, diligence findings, technical and environmental issues, cash flows and returns, risks and mitigants, tax, sustainability and climate, governance and the approval sought.

error.defect_description: Numbers in the memo do not match the final model.

evidence.note: Principals lead investment memoranda. Times are the author's estimates for a mid-sized real estate, infrastructure or energy deal.

steps.name: Review and edit the memo
steps.description: The director reads the draft, checks key numbers against the model, rewrites the thesis and risk sections and sends it back with comments or passes it to the group head.

evidence.note: Times are the author's estimates for a mid-sized real estate, infrastructure or energy deal.

steps.name: Review the memo with the group head
steps.description: The group head reads the memo, tests the thesis, partner and price with the team and decides whether to take it to the department review.

evidence.note: Times are the author's estimates for a mid-sized real estate, infrastructure or energy deal.

steps.name: Check approval authority and required sign-offs
steps.description: A business management associate checks the deal size against the Investment Management Authorities to confirm the approving body, and checks that tax, legal, sustainability and climate sections and sign-offs are present.

control.basis: Investment Management Authorities set by the CEO: transaction approval authorities

evidence.note: Investment Management Authorities set transaction approval authorities for department and group committees.

steps.name: Present at the department investment review
steps.description: The deal team presents to the department head and group heads, answers questions and records the endorsement or required changes before the item goes to Risk and the Portfolio Execution Committee.

control.basis: Investment Management Authorities: department-level committee review

evidence.note: Department-level committee review under the Investment Management Authorities before PEC.

steps.name: Submit the memo to Risk and the committee secretariat
steps.description: The associate files the final memo, model and appendices in the memo repository and sends them to the risk team and the Portfolio Execution Committee secretariat for the next agenda.

evidence.note: PEC reviews new investments with an independent risk opinion. Times are the author's estimates for a mid-sized real estate, infrastructure or energy deal.

exceptions.name: Model rework after review
exceptions.description: The senior associate sends the model back for changes to rent, regulated return or capital assumptions.

exceptions.name: Technical or environmental red flag
exceptions.description: Advisers find deferred capital needs, contamination or permit and concession gaps, and the group head drops the deal.

exceptions.name: Lost in the auction or partner walks
exceptions.description: The seller narrows the field, halts the sale or the partner withdraws.

exceptions.name: Memo rewrite
exceptions.description: The director, group head, authority check or department review sends the memo back for changes.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from screening approval to memo submitted or deal dropped
benchmarks.population: Real estate, infrastructure and energy deals in deep diligence at a large pension investor

evidence.note: Author's reading: auction round 2 runs 4 to 6 weeks and negotiations a further 6 to 8 weeks; renewable energy diligence routinely takes three months or more. Real assets diligence is assumed somewhat longer than the 45-day reading used for direct private equity.

benchmarks.unit: share of deep-diligence deals that close
benchmarks.population: 79 PE investors surveyed (applied to real assets by the organisation file)

evidence.note: 6.1 closes per 23.7 deals in deep diligence.

benchmarks.population: Phase I environmental site assessments under All Appropriate Inquiries

benchmarks.unit: share of F2021 real estate investment activity
benchmarks.population: Real Estate group, excluding listed real estate

evidence.note: More than 98%.

pain_points.description: Technical, environmental and market reports take weeks and arrive late in the phase, so deals are often dropped only after most of the work is done.
Long-term cash flow models over 10 to 30 years are built in spreadsheets and go through several review rounds.

evidence.note: Author's judgment.

pain_points.description: Partner and co-investor negotiations on governance and promote run in parallel with diligence and depend on the other side's timetable.
Tax and sustainability inputs come from other teams and the memo waits for them.
Memo drafting and edits by several levels take one to three weeks.

evidence.note: Author's judgment.

assumptions: The process starts when the group head accepts a screening memo and ends at memo submission; first-round bids, the risk review, committee approval and closing negotiations are other processes.

Volume follows the process map (25 deals a month in deep diligence). This looks high: Real Assets held 179 investments in F2020 and 204 in F2021, and much real estate investment is follow-on capital with existing partners rather than new deep-diligence deals.
About 40% of deals are platforms or operating companies that get a Portfolio Value Creation review; the rest are assets or joint ventures run by partners.
Branch shares are set so that about 55% of deals reach a memo, 30% are dropped by the team and 12% are lost, consistent with the published funnel (26% of deep-diligence deals close).
All deals are treated as needing Portfolio Execution Committee approval; small follow-ons within department authority would stop at the department review.

Hands-on times count focused work only; deal teams also spend unrecorded time on calls and travel. Adviser fees are not in the labour cost. At 25 deals a month the hands-on time implies about 45 FTE and the roles state about 42 FTE, about a sixth of the 252 Real Assets staff, which is another sign that the process map volume is high.

The simulated median (about 60 days) is close to the 55-day benchmark reading; the simulated 90th percentile (about 77 days) is below the 100-day reading because the simulator draws each wait independently and does not reproduce deals that stall for months on regulatory or partner issues.

ra_smd, ra_bm, legal_counsel and compliance_officer are organisation roles that the process map does not list for this process; they are added because the department review, authority check, legal work and watch list need them.

The external advisers' reports, the tax structure memo and the ESG assessment are listed as inputs rather than triggers because they arrive during a case that the screening memo starts; the process map lists them under triggered_by.
Loaded costs per hour are the organisation file's (total compensation scaled to F2022 personnel expense, times an overhead factor of 1.25, divided by 1,950 hours).
